data.description:
## Context / Problem
Automated bug filers (canary red transitions, heartbeat, binding-drift) can spam duplicates, file on single flakes, or silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces).

## Approach
Per OSS practice (PyTorch DISABLED-test bot, Flutter flake bot, Sentry fingerprinting, Alertmanager 'for:'): dedup via stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day; templated body (check name, first-red time, run URL, failing-output tail, workflow path) with abort-if-empty-detail; recovery comment on green; close left to agents. USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS: (a) audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit this same pattern; (b) document the bug-creation contract for automation — exact rebar create args, exit codes, dedup search command, REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var — so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create.

## Scope
- canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic (coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent)
- docs: bug-creation contract page
- audit table of every auto-file site in the change description

## Testing
Filer logic unit tests: first red -> no ticket; second consecutive red -> one ticket with template fields; third red same day -> comment not new ticket; green -> recovery comment; empty detail -> abort with loud log, no hollow ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All audited auto-file sites use the dedup+threshold+template pattern (audit table enumerates them).
- [ ] Bug-creation contract documented and referenced by every filer.
- [ ] Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above.
- [ ] detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).
data.title: Canary auto-file hardening: dedup pattern, all-site audit, bug-creation contract doc
